content.title: Empower teachers, improve learning outcomes
content.summary: Educational Research Conference convenes Tanzania stakeholders to share best practice

media.caption: Education stakeholders having a group discussion in one of the plenary sessions during the 'Utafiti Elimu Tanzania' conference held at the Aga Khan University in Tanzania

content.text: Researchers and education stakeholders are advocating for increased Teacher Continuous Professional Development (TCPD) programmes to improve skills an d welfare of teachers in Tanzania primary schools.

In a conference hosted by the Aga Khan University, experts say building a strong curriculum, measurement of learning, alignment between systems in education, supporting and adaptive approach to teachers are the five areas that need commitment.

"Teachers are trained on the new Competency Based Curriculum, but they have reservations and low self-efficacy. Their reservations are the cause of misalignment in the education system because what students will be tested in exams is not what the teachers were expected to deliver to them," said Dr Richard Shukia, a researcher at the University of Dar es Salaam.

The Utafiti Elimu Tanzania Conference brought together over 150 education stakeholders to discuss how best to improve learning across four themes: Teacher Continuous Professional Development, inclusion, school safety and gender, data for decision making and EdTech strategy.

"As education stakeholders we are discussing how to simplify the work of learning and teaching by teachers," said Dr Jane Rarieya, interim dean at the Institute for Educational Development, East Africa, IED EA.
The Institute plans to perform surveys by tracking teaching and learning of teachers to improve teacher curriculum-based competence.

Dr Winston Massam, faculty at IED EA said, "We will observe them, talk to them, ask them questions and discuss how we can help. But also, to ensure that teachers continue to learn, we are setting up an online platform where all the learning tools and what is being taught to the teachers can be seen, they can revise and learn," he said.
Participants also gave recommendations on interventions to support policy- and decision-makers in implementing investment in education.
The conference was organized by the Aga Khan University in partnership with Aga Khan Foundation, British Council, EdTech Hub and the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office in Tanzania.
